name: OxfordVR gameChange

best_for: and clinicians treating severe agoraphobia in patients with psychotic disorders

short_description: NHS-approved automated VR cognitive therapy for severe agoraphobia in patients with psychosis, featuring a virtual coach guiding exposure to everyday situations
long_description: gameChange is an automated VR cognitive therapy program developed by Oxford University, Oxford VR, and multiple NHS Trusts, recommended for use in NHS mental health services for treating severe agoraphobia in patients with psychosis. It represents the first-ever VR treatment approved for NHS mental health services. The program enables largely housebound patients with agoraphobia to safely practice re-entering everyday situations through immersive VR environments. A virtual coach guides patients through CBT-based exposure therapy, eliminating the need for a real therapist during sessions. Clinical trials led by Professor Daniel Freeman showed significant reductions in avoidance and distress, with patients who were most severely affected experiencing the largest benefits, including being able to undertake activities they had previously found unthinkable.

faqs.a: gameChange is an automated VR cognitive therapy program for treating severe agoraphobia in patients with psychosis. It's the first VR treatment approved for NHS mental health services.
Patients use VR to safely practice re-entering everyday situations with guidance from a virtual coach. The automated CBT-based therapy doesn't require a real therapist during sessions.
gameChange was developed by Oxford University, Oxford VR, Oxford Health NHS Foundation Trust, and nine NHS Trusts, led by Professor Daniel Freeman's 20+ years of clinical VR research.
gameChange treats adults with severe agoraphobia who have psychotic disorders. It's particularly effective for patients who are largely housebound and have the most severe symptoms.
